newsitem.title: USA: CS First Boston faces SEC action over Orange Cnty.
newsitem.headline: CS First Boston faces SEC action over Orange Cnty.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has told CS First Boston that it plans to bring fraud charges against the firm in connection with Orange County, Calif., bonds, according to bond documents.

The commission has authorized the filing of a civil enforcement action against CS First Boston, alleging violations of the anti-fraud statutes of the federal securities laws, according to Orange County documents, obtained by Reuters late on Monday.

The disclosure about CS First Boston was the first indication that the SEC had authorized enforcement action against a firm involved in Orange County bond offerings. The disclosure also suggested the SEC was now close to acting.
A spokesman for CS First Boston, a unit of CS Holding, said the firm would not comment at this time.
SEC associate regional director of enforcement in Los Angeles, Sandra Harris, also declined to comment.
As previously reported, the SEC has been investigating CS First Boston's due diligence as underwriter of county taxable pension obligation bonds, issued just before Orange County declared bankruptcy.

Orange County issued about $320 million of taxable pension bonds on September 28, 1994. The pension bonds were underwritten by CS First Boston, which served as lead underwriter, and by co-underwriters Kidder, Peabody & Co. and Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp.

Jones, Day, Reavis & Pogue was bond counsel for the pension bonds, while Stradling, Yocca, Carlson & Rauth served as underwriters' counsel. O'Brien Partners Inc was the financial adviser, according to county records.
Last year, CS First Boston received a so-called Wells notice, informing the firm that SEC staff intended to recommend that enforcement action be taken against the firm.

According to county documents released Monday, CS First Boston (CSFB) has since been advised that the commission "has authorized the filing of a civil enforcement action against CSFB alleging violations of Section 17(a) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and sections 10(b) and 15(c) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934."
According to the county documents, CS First Boston told the county that the firm "believes it has meritorious defenses to any such SEC action and intends to defend it vigorously."
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion. It emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.
Soon after the county declared bankruptcy, the SEC initiated a sweeping investigation of its massive borrowings.

The SEC has already filed complaints against the county's former treasurer and assistant treasurer, alleging they made misleading statements in the offer and sale of more than $2.1 billion of municipal securities.

In connection with those complaints, the SEC said in court papers that the official statements for the pension bonds contained "material mistatements and omissions" regarding the county's investment strategy and financial condition.
As previously reported, SEC staff has also been investigating several local governments in connection with the bankruptcy as well as several other bond professionals, including Merrill Lynch & Co..
